description: Cache fetched filings locally by accession number so that repeated operations on the same filing don't require re-downloading. Cache should be stored on local filesystem and be clearable/bypassable programmatically. Cut from Epic 1 per review feedback -- not needed for initial library.
title: Filing Cache: Local caching of fetched EDGAR filings

description: Provide an API to search/list available filings by company (ticker or CIK), filing type, and date range. Would wrap the SEC submissions API at data.sec.gov/submissions/. This is out of scope for Epic 1 (the diff library accepts specific accession numbers) but will be needed for the web app (Epic 2) or as a standalone utility. The SEC provides a free JSON API at data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK{padded-cik}.json that returns filing history including accession numbers, dates, form types, and primary document filenames.
title: Filing Discovery: Search and list available filings for a company

description: LLM-powered chat panel with filing-aware Q&A. Users can ask questions about the diff and filings with context-aware responses that reference source text. See .specs/epic-3-chat/PRD.md for full PRD (TBD).
title: LLM Chat Panel

description: Standalone library that fetches SEC filings from EDGAR, parses them into a structured document model, and computes structured diffs between two filings. This is the core engine that all downstream consumers (web app, chat, programmatic users) depend on. See .specs/epic-1-library/PRD.md for full PRD.
title: SEC Filing Diff Library

description: Write the architecture document for Epic 1 (SEC Filing Diff Library). This doc should cover: language/runtime choice, project structure, HTML parsing library selection, diff algorithm approach (Myers, patience, or custom for section alignment), source mapping strategy (byte offsets vs DOM node references vs both), API surface design (fetch_filing, parse_filing, diff_filings), error handling strategy, and testing approach. Should also document the filing agent HTML pattern analysis plan (DFIN, Toppan Merrill, Workiva). This task must be completed before implementation begins.
title: Write architecture document

description: Set up the Nx monorepo structure per the architecture doc (section 1). Create: pnpm-workspace.yaml, nx.json, root package.json, apps/ directory, libs/edgar-diff-lib/ with package.json, tsconfig.json, vitest.config.ts, project.json, and src/index.ts barrel. Configure Nx enforce-module-boundaries lint rule for client/parser/diff import constraints. Install core dev dependencies: typescript, vitest, @js-temporal/polyfill, htmlparser2. Verify 'nx test edgar-diff-lib' runs (even if no tests yet).
title: Scaffold Nx monorepo

description:
Set phase to design-complete

Reason: Design document PR merged
title: State change: phase → design-complete

description: Create root package.json (private, packageManager pinned), pnpm-workspace.yaml (packages: apps/*, libs/*), .npmrc (shamefully-hoist=false, public-hoist-pattern for types/eslint), and nx.json with plugin registrations (@nx/js/typescript, @nx/vitest/plugin, @nx/eslint/plugin), namedInputs, targetDefaults, and caching config. Install nx and @nx/* plugins as root devDependencies.
title: Initialize workspace root

description: Create tsconfig.base.json with shared compiler options (target ES2022, module/moduleResolution nodenext, strict, composite, incremental, declarationMap). Create root tsconfig.json as solution-style references hub listing all projects. These provide the foundation for project references and incremental type checking.
title: Set up TypeScript configuration

description: Create libs/edgar-diff-lib/ with: package.json (name @edgar-diff/lib, exports field restricting public API to barrel, workspace:* ready, nx tags), tsconfig.json extending base with project references, tsconfig.lib.json excluding tests, src/index.ts empty barrel, and directory stubs for tests/unit, tests/integration/fixtures, tests/fuzz, spikes/source-mapping, spikes/diff-algorithm. Install library dependencies: htmlparser2, @js-temporal/polyfill.
title: Create edgar-diff-lib package skeleton

description: Create vitest.config.ts in libs/edgar-diff-lib/. Environment: node. Include pattern: tests/**/*.{test,spec}.ts. Use vite-tsconfig-paths plugin for monorepo path resolution. Point coverage output to workspace-level coverage/ directory. Verify nx test edgar-diff-lib runs successfully (0 tests, 0 failures).
title: Configure Vitest for edgar-diff-lib

description: Create eslint.config.mjs at workspace root. Configure import/no-restricted-paths (or equivalent) to enforce intra-library module boundaries: client cannot import from parser or diff, parser cannot import from diff, diff cannot import from client. Verify nx lint edgar-diff-lib succeeds with boundary rules active.
title: Configure ESLint with module boundary rules

description: Run all verification criteria from the design doc: pnpm install succeeds, nx test edgar-diff-lib runs vitest (0 tests), nx typecheck edgar-diff-lib succeeds, nx lint edgar-diff-lib succeeds with boundary rules, nx graph renders the project. Confirm directory structure matches architecture doc section 1. Confirm package.json exports field restricts API to barrel.
title: Verify scaffold end-to-end

description:
Changed phase from design-complete to implementing

Reason: Starting scaffold implementation
title: State change: phase → implementing

description: vitest.config.ts has passWithNoTests: true to allow the scaffold to pass with an empty test suite. Once the first real test file is added (likely during US-1.1 or Spike A), remove this flag so that an empty test run is treated as a failure — catching broken include patterns or deleted test files.
title: Remove passWithNoTests once first test is added

description: Validate that htmlparser2 startIndex/endIndex values provide accurate character-level positions on real SEC HTML. Per architecture doc section 9. Scope: Fetch one real 10-K filing from EDGAR. Build a minimal SAX-based parser using htmlparser2's DomHandler. Identify 5 section boundaries. Verify html.slice(node.startIndex, node.endIndex) captures expected content. Test with multi-byte characters. Deliverable: spikes/source-mapping/ with runnable TypeScript and NOTES.md documenting character-vs-byte behavior, CDATA/comment anomalies, parse time, API stability. Success criteria: All 5 offset checks pass, multi-byte behavior documented, parse time < 500ms. Fallback: two-pass with linkedom + string scanning. Time box: 2 days.
title: Spike A: Source mapping prototype

description: Validate section alignment quality and patience-diff output on real filing pairs. Per architecture doc section 9. Scope: Two consecutive 10-K filing pairs from two different companies. Implement custom section aligner with Jaro-Winkler similarity. Apply patience diff at paragraph level via the diff npm package. Compare against naive Myers. Deliverable: spikes/diff-algorithm/ with runnable TypeScript and NOTES.md documenting section alignment accuracy, optimal Jaro-Winkler threshold, paragraph diff quality, performance, patience-vs-Myers edge cases. Success criteria: >90% section alignment accuracy, meaningful paragraph diffs, <2s per pair. Fallback: add TF-IDF on section content as secondary signal. Time box: 2 days.
title: Spike B: Diff algorithm prototype

description: Collect 10-15 sample 10-K filings from diverse large-cap filers. Per architecture doc section 6. For each filing, document HTML patterns used for section headings: element types (h1-h4, p, div), inline styles (bold, uppercase, font-size), CSS classes, structural conventions (TOC presence, page breaks). Commit findings to .specs/epic-1-library/html-patterns.md as a structured catalog. This informs the heuristic section-extractor design.
title: Catalog HTML heading patterns from sample filings

description: Implement EDGAR client to fetch a specific SEC filing by accession number. Accepts an accession number (e.g., 0000320193-23-000106). Retrieves the primary HTML document from EDGAR Archives. Returns raw HTML content along with filing metadata (CIK, form type, filing date, accession number). Includes a proper User-Agent header as required by SEC (format: 'Company Name email@domain.com'). Filing URL pattern: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/{CIK}/{accession-number-no-dashes}/{primary-document-filename}
title: US-1.1: Fetch a filing by accession number

description: Implement rate limiting in the EDGAR HTTP client. Enforces maximum 10 requests/second to EDGAR endpoints. Backs off on 429 or 503 responses. Rate limiting is implemented within the library's HTTP layer so callers don't need to manage it externally. Should provide a configurable HTTP client with sensible defaults (built-in rate limiter) while allowing callers to inject their own client if they need different behavior (e.g., a shared rate limiter across multiple library instances).
title: US-1.2: Respect SEC rate limits

description: Implement filing parser that converts raw HTML into a structured document model with source mappings. Identifies standard 10-K sections (Items 1, 1A, 1B, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 7A, 8, 9, 9A, 9B, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15). Handles common HTML patterns for section headings (h-tags, bold paragraphs, font tags, uppercase text). Produces a document tree: Document > Section > Subsection > Content blocks (paragraphs, tables, lists). Each node includes source location references (byte offsets or DOM node identifiers) pointing back to the original HTML. Source mappings enable downstream consumers to overlay diff highlights on the original HTML rendering. Handles filings from major filing agents (Donnelley Financial Solutions, Toppan Merrill, Workiva). Risk signal: if more than 3 distinct HTML pattern families are needed, consider splitting parser into its own epic.
title: US-1.3: Parse filing into structured sections with source mappings

description: Implement table parser that extracts HTML tables into a structured row/column model. Extracts HTML tables into a row/column data structure. Preserves header rows and column labels. Handles merged cells (colspan/rowspan) gracefully. Retains numeric values as numbers where detectable. Each cell includes a source mapping back to its position in the original HTML. Risk signal: if table parsing requires filing-agent-specific logic for more than 2 agents, consider splitting.
title: US-1.4: Parse tables into structured representations

description: Implement section-level diffing that aligns sections across two filings. Matches sections across filings by heading text similarity. Identifies added sections (present in new filing only), removed sections (present in old filing only), modified sections (present in both, content differs), and unchanged sections. Handles renamed sections (e.g., 'Risk Factors' -> 'Risk Factors and Uncertainties'). Handles reordered sections (sections that moved position but are otherwise unchanged or modified). Handles subsection-level matching within matched sections.
title: US-1.5: Compute section-level diff between two parsed filings

description: Implement paragraph-level diffing within matched sections. Within matched sections, aligns paragraphs and detects additions, deletions, and modifications. For modified paragraphs, computes sentence-level diffs to show what changed within the paragraph. Handles paragraph reordering without marking everything as changed. Diff output includes source mappings so that changes can be rendered as overlays/highlights on the original HTML.
title: US-1.6: Compute paragraph-level diffs within matched sections

description: Implement table-level diffing at the cell level. Matches tables across filings by position and header similarity. Computes cell-by-cell diffs for matched tables. Identifies added/removed rows and columns. Highlights changed cell values.
title: US-1.7: Compute table-level diffs

description: Integrate outputs of US-1.5 through US-1.7 into a single coherent structured diff. Diff is returned as a structured object, not rendered text. Includes metadata: accession numbers, filing dates, form type, CIK. Each section diff includes the section heading, change type (added/removed/modified/unchanged/reordered), and content diffs. Paragraph diffs within sections include source mappings to both old and new filing HTML. Table diffs are included within their containing sections. Serializable to JSON for storage or transmission. Output format supports rendering diff highlights as overlays on the original HTML documents.
title: US-1.8: Produce a structured diff output

description: Web application with side-by-side diff viewer, section navigation, and AI-generated change summary. Consumes the library from Epic 1. See .specs/epic-2-web-app/PRD.md for full PRD (TBD).
title: Diff Viewer Web Application

description: Detect whether a filing has inline XBRL (iXBRL) data and use XBRL tags to improve section boundary detection and identify financial figures in tables. Fall back to HTML-only parsing when XBRL is unavailable. This was originally US-1.7 in Epic 1 but was scoped out per review feedback. Should be its own epic or added to a future epic.
title: XBRL Support: Parse and leverage XBRL/iXBRL data for improved accuracy
